quote.text: To see what is in front of one's nose needs a constant struggle.
quote.author: George Orwell, "In Front of Your Nose," Tribune (22 March 1946)

macro.title: What It Means — VWRA, Bonds, Gold & BTC

reads.label: VWRA (held)
reads.text: two-sided into the Fed — a Warsh hold plus Oman de-escalation is relief; a hike or resumed strikes cracks the eggshells. Thursday's earnings are the bigger single-week swing than the Fed.

reads.label: Global bonds (held)
reads.text: the enemy is a hike plus sticky inflation plus the oil premium, all pressing the front end; hedged exposure cushions the firm dollar.

reads.label: Gold (read only)
reads.text: the cleanest hedge here, bid by both war-premium and stagflation-lite.

reads.label: Bitcoin (read only)
reads.text: trading as high-beta risk, not gold's twin — ETF outflows and a fearful tape say defensive positioning. The two he holds stay VWRA and global bonds; the two he only reads stay gold and BTC.

stories.headline: A Billion Views, and a Week to Go
stories.dek: Spider-Man: Brand New Day opens Friday to what trackers already call the biggest debut of 2026. Its trailer became the first in history to cross a billion views — and did it in four days. The spread on the forecast, though, is the honest tell.

stories.headline: The Planet We Filed as Dead
stories.dek: New 3D simulations suggest some of Venus's giant rift valleys formed recently — and may still be widening today. We needed thirty-year-old radar and a new supercomputer model to notice the world next door might still be tearing itself open.

stories.headline: Check Your Connections Before You Book
stories.dek: The Gulf disruption reaches the departures board this weekend, a rail pass gets pricier but only if you buy it the old way, and Changi names the next places it wants to fly. A brisk read for anyone with a trip in the diary.

stories.headline: The Guns Go Quiet, and Oman Lands in Tehran
stories.dek: Friday's order was the one that hadn't come in thirteen nights: hold. As an Omani delegation flew into Tehran to talk Hormuz "mechanisms," the war paused — not because either side had bent, but because both, for a night, chose to let the mediator breathe.

stories.headline: The Tariff You Cannot Appeal
stories.dek: The 12.5% duty landed Thursday; by the weekend the manufacturers were surveying their own exposure and rejecting the label that justified it. The awkward part is that the number was set by category, not by evidence — which is exactly what makes it hard to argue down.

stories.headline: Turf City Opens Its Book
stories.dek: Dunearn House, the first private condo in the Bukit Timah masterplan, took bookings on Saturday at around three thousand dollars a square foot. Whether it sold out is a number we are holding until a named source confirms it — because scarcity, not a market turn, is what a first-mover really tests.

stories.headline: The Verdicts Arrive Before the Weights
stories.dek: Kimi K3's open weights still land Monday. But the first independent assessments came in over the weekend, and they cut against the launch charts: below the frontier on offensive-cyber tasks, unable to stop itself trying anyway, and hiding a hallucination rate that doubled.

stories.headline: Named, Framed, and You Still Can't Wear Them
stories.dek: The hands-on reviews arrived after Unpacked, and firmed up three things about Samsung's smart glasses: an official name, two fashion-house frames — and that the 2026 model has no display, no price, and no date beyond "fall."

stories.headline: The Assistant That Never Phones Home
stories.dek: You can now run a thirty-billion-parameter voice assistant inside Home Assistant with not one byte leaving the house. The catch is the one the community keeps relearning: on the wrong hardware it thinks at walking pace, and the wall paddle still wins.

stories.headline: The Tokyo Watch Run Has a Closing Date
stories.dek: The instant tax-free discount that made Japan a pilgrimage through the weak-yen years ends on 1 November. From then you pay full price and chase a refund at the departure gate — which quietly changes what the trip is actually worth.

stories.headline: It May Be Puberty, Not the Phone
stories.dek: A new study finds the adolescent slide to later, shorter sleep tracks pubertal stage more tightly than age — so an early-maturing eleven-year-old can already be running a teenager's body clock in a child's routine. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Week Ahead
stories.headline: Fed Versus Oil, and the Question Is Still "Hike?"
stories.dek: The barrel round-tripped a hundred dollars again on peace-talk hopes; the dollar sits near a three-week high; and Wednesday's Fed meeting carries a live hike tail, not a cut. A quiet Sunday reading before a loud week. Market explanation, not investment advice.

stories.headline: The Buffer Is Shared Time — If You Both Mean It
stories.dek: A long diary study finds what slows a marriage's decline isn't grand gestures but ordinary shared hours — and the protection only holds when both partners are genuinely invested. Going through the motions doesn't buy it.

stories.headline: Fifteen Minutes a Day, and More Buys Nothing
stories.dek: A thirty-year study pins the mortality-optimal dose of lifting at ninety to a hundred and twenty minutes a week — and finds no extra survival benefit above it. The optimizer's instinct to do more is, for once, the wrong one. General information, not medical advice.

stories.headline: The Autumn Calendar Comes Into Focus
stories.dek: Race week now has its full bill, Mid-Autumn lights the Gardens, and a run of concerts firms up — the dated, bookable agenda for a reader planning the next three months.

stories.headline: The Backpackers of Huaqiangbei
stories.dek: A generation of young Chinese has started to vacation inside the largest electronics market on earth — arriving with empty backpacks, leaving with component hauls, and vlogging the whole thing. It is a small, strange story that the West, which has written about this place for a decade, has managed not to see.
